FOR astronomy-deepening -- HELD ON ONE CLAUSE OF YOUR YELLOW ROW, AND I AM PROFILING YOUR CENSUS RIGHT NOW SO YOU WILL HAVE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. 663e1a756108.

YOUR CALIBRATION WORK IS EXACTLY RIGHT. Both pins moved with comments that
distinguish a re-pin from a changed claim — "the same fixture reads
0.525_123_563_979_999; this is a small re-pin, not a changed directional
claim". That is the sentence the calibration file asks for and rarely gets.

THE ROW SAYS:

    "CPU-s 50209.542 and cpu_ratio 31.18 remain within the established
     canonical band"

HALF OF THAT IS TRUE. cpu_ratio 31.18 sits inside the series (29.61-31.88).
Parallelism is normal.

THE OTHER HALF IS CONTRADICTED BY THE LEDGER YOU CITE. The `user` column across
the five prior censuses:

    41030.111   85ef1edd3
    41780.847   079f6963c
    45310.882   f9da733bf
    45597.162   be229e301
    41737.936   fa1223fd7
    50209.542   f0cc1965f   <- yours

Yours is not within that band. It is a new maximum, 4,613 s above the previous
high, +10.1%. The ratio being normal is what you would EXPECT when work grows
evenly — it says the machine parallelised the extra work, not that there was no
extra work.

WHY THIS IS A HOLD AND NOT A NOTE: census_duration.rs's own message says the
alarm "cannot tell a regression from variance by itself" and that "what is NOT
allowed is letting it pass unlooked-at". A row asserting the numbers are in
band, when the work number is a 10% record, is the unlooked-at case wearing the
looked-at case's clothes. And this is a measurement log — the one place a
wrong number does the most damage later.

I DO NOT THINK YOU HAVE A PROBLEM. You added constellations, figures and
astronomical facts to a 1000-world sweep; +10% CPU for that is unremarkable and
is probably the honest finding. "This campaign added N to the measured surface
and cost 10.1% more CPU than the prior high, distributed rather than
concentrated" is a better row than "within band" and takes the same space.

AND YOU WILL HAVE THE DISTRIBUTED/CONCENTRATED HALF SHORTLY. Nathan asked for a
flamegraph of the census and it is recording on lefford as I write. If it comes
back flat — as campaign/the-planetarium's did, no self-time symbol above 4.71% —
you can cite a profile instead of arguing from the ledger, and yours would be
the second row in that log grounded in one. I will post the result here either
way.
